raw_results.scope:
Compare ordinary TCG and Sim through the same complete serial milestone.

All rows boot identical stock kernel and initramfs bytes. The primary interval
starts before QEMU spawn and ends when the common socket reader receives the
complete pre-request token. It includes emulator startup, QMP setup and boot;
protocol allocation and post-marker diagnostics are outside the interval.

Ordinary TCG without icount, ordinary TCG with 1 ns per instruction, and Sim
with 50 ps per instruction use different execution contracts. Their same-workload
boot latency comparison is not a measurement of equal-instruction overhead.
Sim's authenticated native stop, full RAM, registers and timer witness are
qualified separately after the common marker. Stock post-marker QMP stops are
not exact token coordinates. CPU accounting endpoints are recorded per row.

Build the new guest and driver with the AOS phase2.tcgLinuxSerialGuest and
phase2.tcgLinuxSerialPerformanceDriver targets using local builders. Pass each
row explicitly as --row LABEL MODE QEMU_BINARY PLUGIN_OR_DASH. Modes are tcg,
tcg-icount and sim; ordinary TCG takes '-' for the plugin. No plugins are loaded
in ordinary TCG rows, even when the emulator supports them. Repeated rounds
rotate row positions and then reverse the rotations. Every start, exit, stream,
raw result and failed attempt is retained; no failed trial is retried or replaced.

lifecycleAudit.machinePublication: Only system/vl.c:2215 assigns current_machine; machine creation precedes accelerator configuration.
lifecycleAudit.acceleratorPublication: Only accel_init_machine assigns MachineState.accelerator: publication before init callback, clearing before unref on failure.
lifecycleAudit.classNameLifetime: Concrete shipped names are assigned in class_init; no runtime mutation found. Custom classes may have NULL name: initialization remains valid and the new predicate returns false. Exact-equivalence applies to immutable non-NULL initialized names.
lifecycleAudit.oldContract: current_accel_name/current_accel require a valid current machine/current accelerator; current_accel_name may return NULL for a nameless custom class. NULL machine/instance calls and strcmp of a NULL name previously had no defined result.
lifecycleAudit.newContract: current_accel_is_sim explicitly returns false with NULL machine, NULL accelerator, or a successfully initialized class with NULL name. Failure-clear before independent retry remains safe.
lifecycleAudit.resetRestoreFork: Reset/rebuild_guest and VMState retain the accelerator instance; no VMState serialization of AccelState/classification. A real fork inherits the instance memory.
lifecycleAudit.exactMatching: Exact display-name equality to sim, independent of inherited type; all concrete names plus arbitrary case/prefix/suffix names covered.
lifecycleAudit.userSupport: Getter is defined in accel-system.c only; changed callers are system-only, and accel-user.c/current_accel_name remain unchanged.
lifecycleAudit.unchangedConsumers: Actual diagnostic names, unrelated device comparisons, API/startup paths and cpu-exec BQL fences retained.

positiveCoverage: Actual production AccelState, AccelClass, AccelGdbConfig, enum and QOM class macro declarations extracted unchanged.
Actual init, current_accel, current_accel_is_sim and current_accel_name bodies extracted unchanged.
All changed predicate bodies plus complete RR timer guard and icount limit/budget/run preparation execute unchanged.
102 mode/name/ancestry cases; zero deadline precise/adaptive/off budget paths; replay path and noquantum guard order; 90000 hot queries avoid repeated QOM/name work.
Early NULL machine and NULL accelerator; failed sim callback/retry tcg/new sim; retained old instance selection; actual fork identity and result continuity.
Successful nameless custom-class initialization overwrites an initially true classification, returns false during its callback, and leaves current_accel_name returning NULL.
boundedProviders: QOM class lookup/cast and superclass membership, object unref/compat effects, machine shell, CPU field shell, timer sinks, replay locks, clock deadlines/rounding, fault-registry presence and dispatch registration.
nativeCoverageLimitations: No native QOM registration/type inheritance or native machine reset/VMState stream executes; reset/restore continuity depends on audited unchanged instance identity.
No full emulator build, translated guest, scheduling, clocks, TB shape/chaining/count, remote build or profile executes.

The native-header-dependent lifecycle-projection fixture and vcpu-service-time C unit cannot run without absent generated config-host.h; their changed production predicates execute in the new extracted-body proof.
